**North Atrium Cafeteria | Reusable container return trial**

Beginning Monday, staff who buy lunch in a reusable container may return it at either collection point beside the north elevators or the main reception desk. Containers returned before 4 P.M. will be washed that evening. Those returned later will be processed the following business day.

During the two-week trial, the usual container deposit will still be charged at checkout. The deposit will be credited automatically to an employee's cafeteria account after the returned container is scanned. Employees should keep the small barcode label attached because the scanner uses it to match the container with the original purchase.

The trial is intended to reduce the number of disposable meal boxes used in the building. If return rates are high enough, two more collection points will be added next month.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the trial?

options.text: To decrease the use of disposable food containers
To extend cafeteria opening hours
To test a new lunch menu
To move cafeteria payments to reception

questions.question_text: What happens after a returned container is scanned?

options.text: The employee receives a paper receipt.
The deposit is credited to the employee's cafeteria account.
The container is sent directly to the kitchen.
The barcode label is removed.

questions.question_text: Why should employees leave the barcode label on the container?

options.text: It shows when the container was washed.
It identifies the collection point.
It allows the return to be matched with the purchase.
It gives the employee a discount on lunch.

questions.question_text: What is implied about a container returned at 5 P.M. on Tuesday?

options.text: It will not qualify for a deposit credit.
It must be taken to the north elevators.
It will be washed on Tuesday evening.
It will be processed on the next business day.

From: Lena Voss, Training Office
To: Branch supervisors
Subject: Revised coaching workshop

The customer-service coaching workshop scheduled for 18 August has been moved from Room 3B to the fourth-floor studio. The original room will be used for an emergency electrical inspection. The workshop still begins at 9:30 A.M., but participants may enter the studio from 9:10 to test the headsets used during role-play exercises.

Please remind participants to bring the service scenario they prepared after last month's online module. We will use those scenarios in pairs before lunch. Printed copies are acceptable, but staff who bring a digital copy should download it to their device beforehand because guest wireless access in the studio is limited.

Supervisors who have not yet submitted attendee names should do so by noon on Friday. The catering order will be finalized that afternoon.

options.text: The original room is needed for an electrical inspection.
The fourth-floor studio has more seating.
The workshop will include a catered lunch.
Participants requested access to headsets.

questions.question_text: What are participants encouraged to do before arriving?

options.text: Print a copy of every role-play scenario.
Download digital materials to their devices.
Submit a catering request.
Complete the online module again.

questions.question_text: What will participants use before lunch?

options.text: A list of catering choices
The studio's wireless network
Service scenarios they prepared earlier
Electrical inspection reports

questions.question_text: Why is Friday noon important to supervisors?

options.text: It is when the workshop begins.
It is when the online module closes.
It is the last time to test the headsets.
It is the deadline for attendee names.

**Harbor View Offices | Lift maintenance schedule**

On Thursday, Lift B will be unavailable from 7 A.M. until approximately 11 A.M. while a contractor replaces its door sensor. Lift A will remain in service, although deliveries using carts should wait until after 9 A.M. to avoid the morning arrival period.

Tenants on floors 2 through 5 may also use the east stairwell. Access cards are required to re-enter office floors from that stairwell. Visitors should therefore remain with their host if they use the stairs.

The contractor will test Lift B several times before returning it to service. Brief movement of the lift during the maintenance window does not mean it is available to passengers. A notice will be removed from the ground-floor doors only after the facilities manager confirms that testing is complete.

questions.question_text: What work will be done on Lift B?

options.text: Its door sensor will be replaced.
Its access-card reader will be moved.
Its passenger capacity will be increased.
Its ground-floor doors will be widened.

questions.question_text: Why are cart deliveries advised to wait until after 9 A.M.?

options.text: Lift A will be tested before 9 A.M.
The building is expected to be busiest earlier in the morning.
Delivery staff cannot use access cards before 9 A.M.
The east stairwell is closed to carts until 9 A.M.

questions.question_text: What must a visitor do when using the east stairwell?

options.text: Leave an access card at reception
Wait until Lift B is moving
Stay with the person hosting the visit
Use only floors 2 and 5

questions.question_text: How will tenants know that Lift B is ready for passengers?

options.text: A contractor will call each office.
The lift will stop moving for ten minutes.
Lift A will be taken out of service.
The notice on the ground-floor doors will be removed.

groups.passage:
**Route planning helps a florist cut missed deliveries**

Aster & Pine, a florist serving three business districts, recently changed how it schedules office deliveries. Previously, drivers received a list arranged by the time each order was placed. That often sent a driver back and forth across the city. During a six-week trial, orders were instead grouped by building zone and by the time customers said someone would be available to receive them.

The change reduced total driving distance by 18 percent. More importantly, the number of second delivery attempts fell sharply because drivers arrived during confirmed reception hours. The company did not buy new routing software. Its dispatch coordinator built the trial using a scheduling feature already included in the firm's order system.

Aster & Pine will keep the new method and add one refinement. Starting next month, customers ordering for large offices will receive a short message asking whether the building has a separate loading entrance. The company expects this information to reduce delays at security desks.

questions.question_text: What problem did the previous scheduling method create?

options.text: Drivers sometimes traveled inefficient routes.
Customers could not choose delivery dates.
Orders were often entered twice.
Drivers were assigned to only one district.

questions.question_text: What contributed to fewer second delivery attempts?

options.text: Drivers were given larger vehicles.
Deliveries were timed for confirmed reception hours.
Customers collected flowers from district depots.
The company hired extra dispatch staff.

questions.question_text: What is indicated about the technology used in the trial?

options.text: It was supplied by a customer.
It was used only to track fuel consumption.
It was already part of the company's order system.
It replaced the company's order system.

questions.question_text: What information will some customers be asked to provide next month?

options.text: The number of employees in the office
The preferred type of flower arrangement
The name of the building security company
Whether the building has a separate loading entrance

From: Conference Operations
To: Registered exhibitors
Subject: Evening access on setup day

The exhibition hall will normally close to exhibitors at 6 P.M. on setup day. Companies that need additional time may request evening access until 8 P.M. Requests must be submitted through the exhibitor portal by 2 P.M. on setup day so that security can prepare an approved-access list.

Only registered exhibitor staff may remain after 6 P.M. Delivery drivers and outside contractors must leave by the normal closing time unless Conference Operations has issued them a separate temporary pass. The loading dock will close at 6:30 P.M., so late-access teams should arrange all large deliveries earlier.

Lighting and basic electrical service will remain available throughout the evening period. Technical support staff, however, leave at 6 P.M. Exhibitors should complete any work requiring venue technicians before then.

questions.question_text: What is the latest time approved exhibitor staff may remain in the hall?

options.text: 8 P.M.
6 P.M.
2 P.M.

questions.question_text: Why must evening-access requests be submitted by 2 P.M.?

options.text: Technical staff need time to inspect each booth.
Security needs time to prepare an approved-access list.
The loading dock requires a delivery schedule.
The exhibitor portal closes for maintenance.

questions.question_text: What must an outside contractor have to remain after 6 P.M.?

options.text: A delivery receipt
A loading-dock reservation
A separate temporary pass
A technician's identification badge

questions.question_text: Which task should exhibitors finish before 6 P.M.?

options.text: Submitting the evening-access request
Using the hall's lighting
Removing registered staff from the hall
Work that requires venue technical support

**Brightpath Office Systems | Printer lease options**

| Plan | Monthly pages included | Service visits | Monthly fee |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core | 3,000 | 2 per year | $145 |
| Plus | 6,000 | 4 per year | $210 |
| Studio | 8,000 | 6 per year | $255 |

All plans include toner delivery. Additional black-and-white pages cost $0.02 each. A service visit requested after the annual allowance is used costs $85. Upgrading to a higher plan is free at a renewal date. Midterm upgrades require a $60 administration fee.

---

From: Minh Rao, Purchasing
To: Brightpath Office Systems
Subject: Renewal for the design annex

Our Core lease for the design annex renews on 1 October. The annex has averaged about 5,400 pages a month since two new project teams moved in. We also used both included service visits by May and paid for one additional visit in July.

For the next lease year, I want a plan that covers our current page volume without routine overage charges and provides at least four service visits. Please confirm the lowest-cost plan that meets both needs. If we change plans at the 1 October renewal, let me know whether any administration charge applies.

questions.question_text: Which plan best meets Minh's stated requirements at the lowest monthly fee?

options.text: Plus
Core
Studio
None of the plans

questions.question_text: Why did the design annex pay for a service visit in July?

options.text: The printer exceeded its monthly page allowance.
The two included Core service visits had already been used.
The lease had expired in May.
Toner delivery was not included in Core.

questions.question_text: What change caused the annex's printing volume to increase?

options.text: A new toner supplier was selected.
The printer was moved to another floor.
Two project teams moved into the annex.
Service visits were reduced.

questions.question_text: What administration fee should apply if the plan changes on 1 October?
If the annex remained on Core and printed 5,400 pages in one month, what would its black-and-white page overage cost for that month?

**Larkspur Distribution | Inter-warehouse transfer schedule**

Transfers confirmed by 11 A.M. are assigned to the next available route below.

| Route | Departure | Destination | Pallet limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Monday 2 P.M. | East Hub | 8 |
| R2 | Tuesday 9 A.M. | North Hub | 12 |
| R3 | Wednesday 1 P.M. | East Hub | 14 |
| R4 | Thursday 10 A.M. | North Hub | 10 |

Hazardous materials require separate authorization and do not count as confirmed until the authorization is attached. Standard transfers may use any open pallet position.

---

**Transfer request 6814**
Submitted Monday at 9:20 A.M.
Destination East Hub
Contents 10 pallets of boxed display stands
Special handling none
Requested arrival by Thursday morning

Status at 10:15 A.M.
R1 has only 6 pallet positions remaining. R3 has 14 positions remaining.

---

From: Inez Kwan, Inventory Manager
To: Dispatch desk
Time: Monday 10:35 A.M.

Please keep request 6814 together rather than splitting it. East Hub is reorganizing the showroom on Thursday afternoon, so arrival before lunch that day is sufficient. If the first East Hub route cannot take the full request, assign it to the next East Hub route. Once assigned, send the route number to the showroom coordinator so they can reserve unloading staff.

questions.question_text: Why can request 6814 be treated as confirmed before 11 A.M.?

options.text: It does not require special handling authorization.
It is going to North Hub.
It contains fewer than eight pallets.
It was submitted on Wednesday.

questions.question_text: Which route should be assigned to request 6814?

options.text: R1
R3
R2
R4

questions.question_text: Why does Inez say that arrival before lunch on Thursday is sufficient?

options.text: The unloading staff work only in the morning.
The transfer was submitted after the daily cutoff.
The showroom reorganization begins Thursday afternoon.
East Hub closes on Wednesday evening.

questions.question_text: What should Dispatch do after assigning the request to a route?

options.text: Reduce the request to six pallets.
Attach hazardous-material authorization.
Move the departure to Thursday morning.
Send the route number to the showroom coordinator.
